articles.summary: For the second year in a row, Archer's Midnight electric air taxi will be featured at the 2026 California International Air Show in Salinas, California, as part of its 'No Roads' flight tour. As Archer's flight test base since 2021, Salinas is the flight tour’s hometown stop. Hundreds of team members from Archer’s engineering, operations, and flight test organizations are expected to celebrate with the community before the flight tour continues on to larger cities in the Bay Area. Midnight recently completed its first stops of the ‘No Roads’ Tour with multiple piloted roundtrip journeys between Salinas Municipal Airport and Hollister Municipal Airport and from Salinas to Monterey. Conducted in close coordination with the FAA, these flights give the public a chance to see the benefits of air taxis firsthand: low noise, zero operating emissions, and the ability to skip over traffic — turning drives of an hour or more into 10–20 minute trips. articles.title: Archer to Showcase Midnight Flights at 2026 California International Air Show as Part of Its 'No Roads' Flight Tour

articles.summary: On Friday, September 4th, Archer’s all-electric Midnight aircraft completed its first stop on its ‘No Roads’ flight tour with a piloted roundtrip journey between Salinas Municipal Airport and Hollister Municipal Airport in California. Both legs took roughly 12 minutes in the air, which by comparison can each take ~40 minutes or more by car. ( Watch Video ) The aircraft reached speeds of 125 mph, cruised at 3,550 feet, and covered over 40 miles roundtrip. The tour, which is being done in close coordination with the FAA, will continue over the coming weeks with planned flights to Monterey, San Martin, San Jose, Oakland, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Texas, and Florida. Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the completion of Midnight’s city-to-city roundtrip flight between Salinas and Hollister, CA - the first stop on the company’s ‘No Roads’ flight tour. articles.summary: Archer’s ‘No Roads’ flight tour will begin in Northern California with a series of city-to-city flights, coming on the heels of more than 70 test flights in August alone and Archer’s recent successful roundtrip flight from Salinas to Monterey. Archer is closely coordinating its ‘No Roads’ tour flights with the FAA. Locations are expected to include Monterey, Hollister, San Martin, San Jose, Oakland, San Francisco and around the Los Angeles area, as well as flights in Texas and Florida. Goal of the tour is to showcase the advantages electric air taxis will bring: low noise, zero operating emissions, and the ability to skip over traffic—featuring flights on routes that can take an hour or more by car, but just 10–20 minutes in the air. The tour is set to advance Archer’s operational readiness for its role as the Official Air Taxi Provider of the LA28 Games and as part of the White House’s eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP). articles.title: Archer Launches ‘No Roads’ Flight Tour As Part Of Its Participation In White House’s Air Taxi Pilot Program and Preparation for LA28 Games

articles.summary: America's Consortium for Electric Skyways (ACES) — launched by Archer Aviation, BETA Technologies and Macquarie Capital — announces plans to bring its interoperable charging network to Texas to support Texas’s Department of Transportation (TxDOT) air taxi operations under the White House's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP). The consortium plans to work with the Texas Department of Transportation over the coming months to identify where aircraft operators plan to fly under the eIPP — and where charging infrastructure should be best located to enable operations. TxDOT was selected for the eIPP program in March 2026 and is positioned to be one of the states leading the way in the rollout of this new technology. TxDOT and ACES have a shared goal of connecting the Texas Triangle (Dallas/Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio and Houston) and rural communities with air taxi networks expanding from each city to extend regional reach. America's Consortium for Electric Skyways (ACES) today
articles.title: Archer, BETA Plan to Bring Air Taxi Charging Infrastructure to Texas to Support TxDOT’s eIPP Operations with America’s Consortium for Electric Skyways

articles.summary: Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the expiration of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the "HSR Act"), with respect to the previously announced agreements pursuant to which Archer will acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries. The expiration of the HSR Act waiting period occurred at 11:59 p.m. EDT on September 18, 2026. The expiration of the HSR Act waiting period satisfies a key condition to closing the transaction. Completion of the transaction remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of other customary closing conditions, including receipt of certain other regulatory approvals, which are underway. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.
